Subject: Nimbus Health — pricing & cache assumptions (post-call recap)

Team — quick post-call write-up from my 11:00am PT discovery with John Hargrove / Sarah Lee at Nimbus Health. High-level: they are building an in-app patient triage assistant (multi-turn chat + some structured output) and are sensitive to both latency and monthly spend. They pushed back on the headline per-token number and asked us to show how caching changes effective unit economics.

Key qualitative notes from the call:
- Use case: real-time patient triage and intake, ~95% of sessions follow a small set of templated workflows (intents), so we expect good prefix reuse.
- Traffic profile: John estimated 2.3M sessions/month; avg tokens per session ~120 output tokens (plus ~20 prompt tokens) — baseline monthly generation tokens ~= 322M tokens (rounded).
- SLA: 99.9% availability; regional (US) hosting required.
- Procurement: they want a 3-month pilot with a target monthly spend range of $8k–$40k (they said $15k ideal).

Michael's back-of-envelope economics (requested by John on the call):
Assumptions I used for the table below:
- Retail (hosted) list price: $24 per 1M generation tokens (we used a conservative figure for negotiation).
- Cache-served tokens marginal cost: assumed $2 per 1M (represents warm-cache KV fetch + infra).
- Effective cost formula: effective $/1M = list_price * (1 - hit_rate) + cache_cost * hit_rate.

Scenarios (effective $/1M tokens):
- 0% hit: 24*(1 - 0) + 2*0 = $24.00 per 1M
- 25% hit: 24*0.75 + 2*0.25 = 18.00 + 0.50 = $18.50 per 1M
- 40% hit: 24*0.60 + 2*0.40 = 14.40 + 0.80 = $15.20 per 1M
- 60% hit: 24*0.40 + 2*0.60 = 9.60 + 1.20 = $10.80 per 1M

Applying to John’s volume (~322M tokens/month) — total monthly cost estimates: (rounded)
- 0% hit: 322 * 24 / 1000 = $7,728
- 25% hit: 322 * 18.5 / 1000 = $5,957
- 40% hit: 322 * 15.2 / 1000 = $4,894
- 60% hit: 322 * 10.8 / 1000 = $3,478

Observations / risk areas:
- Prefix cache sensitivity: if their workflows are templated as they claim, 40%–60% prefix-hit is plausible. If they have highly personalized content, hit rates drop below 25%.
- Session KV vs prefix: session-level KV caching (per active session) helps when conversations are long; prefix cache helps most for repeat entry points across sessions. We should model both.
- Measurement: John asked for a conservative and an optimistic scenario; he explicitly asked that we show a path to ~$10–$12 per 1M effective if possible.

Next steps I propose (internal ask in bold):
1) LAUREN — can you prepare a 1-page pilot quote with three price points that map to conservative/expected/optimistic hit rates (25/40/60) and show the per-month totals for 3 pilot sizes (100M / 300M / 1B tokens)? Use $24 list / $2 cache baseline above and include an optional canary discount (5%) for the pilot. Please include a short note on expected latency differences for cached vs non-cached tokens.
2) PRIYOM — can you pull any similar pilot telemetry or prior deals where we recorded prefix-hit and effective $/1M so we can show precedent (anonymized)?
3) BEN — I plan to offer a technical-runbook session to John/Sarah next week to validate caching approach; can you join and own the KV/cache architecture section?

Attachments from call: John shared a 2-page requirements doc and a spreadsheet with monthly traffic estimates (attached below). I saved both to Drive.

Thanks Michael — good notes. A couple of quick clarifications and a proposed quote structure: 

Clarifications:
- I will assume 24/1M list price for generation tokens and 2/1M cached cost as you used. If legal/finance wants a different list, I’ll swap values but keep the sensitivities the same.
- For the pilot quote I’ll present three tiers tied to hit rates: Conservative (25% hit), Target (40% hit), Stretch (60% hit). Each tier will have a per-1M effective row and monthly totals at the three volume points you requested.

Proposed quote structure (draft bullets):
- Pilot term: 90 days, up to 300M tokens included at pilot price (overage billed at effective rate for chosen tier).
- Price tiers (effective $/1M): Conservative: $18.50 | Target: $15.20 | Stretch: $10.80
- Optional: 5% pilot credit if they sign LOI before the technical runbook session.

I’ll produce the one-pager and sample invoice lines by EOD tomorrow. Ben — I’ll call out the latency delta so John sees expected 1–3ms per-token savings on cache hits (depending on infra); do we have a recent benchmark to cite?

-Lauren

Adding two quick notes from an applied ML / runtime perspective that may help the architecture doc and the demo: 

1) Hit-rate buckets — practical guidance:
- Template-heavy intents (forms, triage flows): expect 45%–65% prefix reuse if templates are canonicalized and prompts are normalized.
- Short freeform replies and patient-specific notes: expect 0%–20% reuse.
- Session-KV (in-memory per session): this is effective for follow-up Q/A within a session; treat expected contribution as +5–15% on top of prefix reuse for long sessions.

2) Measurement plan for pilot (what we should instrument):
- Prefix-hash counts (unique canonical prompts) and count distribution to compute 1st-party hit expectation.
- Token-level origin tagging (cached vs live) so we can report effective $/1M in the pilot dashboard.
- Latency percentile split for cached vs non-cached responses.

I’ll draft a one-page measurement plan and a short checklist for the technical-runbook session.

-Priyom

1) Can you send the 3-tier pilot quote (Conservative/Target/Stretch) in invoice-line format so our Sourcing team can plug into their model?
2) We’d like a short appendix describing how you derive the cache marginal cost ($2/1M) — is that dominated by memory/disk or by additional requests to a cache service?
3) For measurement: happy with token-level tagging. Can we get a sample telemetry dashboard (mock) that shows how you would present effective $/1M over the pilot? Even a screenshot of a template is fine.

Assuming the quote fits within our target $8k–$40k window, we’ll plan for the technical-runbook w/ your team next Wed afternoon.
